Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

facultās

facultās, facultātis f.

noun, third declension

ability, capacity; the means or chance to do something; possibility, means, opportunity (to do something)

In this lexicon

  • ability

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 10.1.11: loquendī facultāte caruērunt; Traupman 28, 149, 267

  • possibility

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Mil. 45: Milōnī manendī nūlla facultās; Caes. BG 1.32.5: fugae facultās

Examples

  • īnfantēs ā mūtīs nūtrīcibus jussū rēgum in sōlitūdine ēducātī, etiamsī verba quaedam ēmīsisse trāduntur, tamen loquendī facultāte caruērunt

    babies brought up in solitude by mute nurses on the orders of kings, though they are said to have uttered some words, still lacked the ability to speakQuint. 10.1.11

    In the entry for ability

  • neque longiōra mihi darī spatia vīvendī volō quam dum erō ad hanc quoque facultātem scrībendī commentandīque idōneus

    and I want no longer span of life than while I am still able to write and take notesGell. praef. 24

    In the entry for ability

  • juvābit tamen rērum gestārum memoriae prīncipis terrārum populī prō virīlī parte et ipsum cōnsuluisse

    still, it will be a pleasure to have done, to the best of my ability, my own part for the memory of the deeds of the foremost people on earthLiv. praef. 3

    In the entry for ability

  • Milōnī manendī nūlla facultās, exeundī nōn causa sōlum sed etiam necessitās fuit

    Milo had no possibility of staying, and for setting out not only a reason but a necessityCic. Mil. 45

    In the entry for possibility

  • ut prīmum potestās data est augendae dignitātis tuae, nihil praetermīsī in tē ōrnandō

    as soon as I had the chance to add to your standing, I left nothing undone to honour youCic. Fam. 10.13.1

    In the entry for possibility

  • proptereā quod reliquīs tamen fugae facultās darētur

    because the rest, at least, had the possibility of flightCaes. BG 1.32.5

    In the entry for possibility
